Low forest-floor perspective beneath a sugar pine old-growth interior, two-hundred-foot deeply furrowed grey-orange trunks of staggered girth rising at irregular angles — one dominant trunk off-center and massive, its neighbors scattered at uneven distances — long pendant cones hanging from upper limbs in dense ornamental clusters, sparse needle-litter and scattered granite slabs flooring the scene between sprawling, asymmetric root flares

Looking straight up through a subalpine larch stand at treeline, weathered pale trunks of uneven thickness rising at irregular, wandering angles — some leaning hard into the prevailing wind, one storm-snapped trunk jutting at a sharp diagonal — above a gold-needle and lichen-crust floor, glacier-polished bedrock slabs emerging between tangled root systems, krummholz crowding the upper canopy fringe, one ragged gap torn open directly overhead
